gaps.sentence: I ___ getting up early because I have done it for years.
gaps.hint: be used to means present familiarity
gaps.explanation: 'Be used to' plus -ing means familiarity with something, here in the present: am used to.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to Greece for our honeymoon, but that was twenty years ago.
gaps.hint: twenty years ago fixes a finished past
gaps.explanation: A finished time expression like 'twenty years ago' demands the past simple: went.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: Look at Sam — he ___ at that stranger again.
gaps.hint: look draws attention to this moment
gaps.explanation: 'Look' draws attention to something happening now, so the present continuous is used: is staring.

gaps.sentence: There ___ a cinema on this corner, but it closed years ago.
gaps.hint: a past state that has ended
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' is also used for past states that no longer exist: used to be.

gaps.sentence: This month they ___ a new wing to the hospital, so some services are elsewhere.
gaps.hint: this month means a temporary current period
gaps.explanation: 'This month' describes a temporary situation around now, so the present continuous fits: are adding.

gaps.sentence: Wait there and I ___ you some aspirin.
gaps.hint: a spontaneous offer at the moment
gaps.explanation: Offers made spontaneously at the moment of speaking use 'will': will get.

gaps.sentence: By the age of thirty, she ___ her own company.
gaps.hint: by the age of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An achievement completed before a past reference point takes the past perfect: had started.
